QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_11

question.text: The 'Clawback' provision in a Category II AIF's Contribution Agreement primarily protects:

answer.text: The manager from adverse tax assessments
Investors, by allowing recovery of carried interest or performance fees paid on early successful exits to offset later failed investments and preserve fund-as-a-whole economics

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes clawback as a mechanism that lets investors recover carried interest or performance fees paid to the manager on early successful exits when later investments fail, so that the manager's carry is ultimately consistent with the fund-as-a-whole economics. The workbook also notes that the manager's ability to refund such amounts matters in practice. The Trap: Option A is unrelated to clawback. Option B describes sponsor liability, a different topic. Option C describes trustee indemnity clauses — a different section of fund documentation. Note: Frame clawback as the investor-protection lever that re-aligns total carry to overall fund performance, not just early wins.
